core_obligations: Reduce to closed points (proof lines 733-742): the blowup is integral, and it suffices to check regularity at closed points; a closed point of the blowup maps to the closed point of the base because the morphism is proper, hence lies on the exceptional divisor.

Conclude by the local equation (proof lines 742-753): the exceptional divisor is an effective Cartier divisor isomorphic to the projective line over the residue field, so a local equation of the divisor at a closed point has quotient isomorphic to the local ring of the projective line at that point, which is regular because the projective line is covered by spectra of polynomial rings; the quotient criterion for regularity of a quotient by a regular element finishes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Show the blowup is integral and reduce regularity to closed points.
Use that a closed point lies on the exceptional divisor and take a local equation.
Apply the quotient criterion for regularity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the blowup of the maximal ideal of a regular local ring of dimension two is an irreducible regular scheme (statement lines 726-732). The proof (proof lines 733-753) reduces regularity to closed points, uses that closed points lie on the exceptional divisor, and applies the quotient criterion with a local equation of the exceptional divisor. H2: a complete short argument in two steps.
